_comment: cloud-ci-affected-set binding workspace-coverage policy (DATA, not code). ADR-0554, converts FRIC-1781310000: the only binding buck2 lane was scoped to //cloud/cloud-ci/..., so code anywhere else could merge broken (PR #651 head cf16525 did not compile yet its buck2 lane was green). ALL repo-specifics live here; the Rust kernel hardcodes no oyatie path and runs on any buck2 repo by editing this pack. full_trigger_patterns are the rdeps-cone ESCAPE classes — graph-semantic files whose blast radius the owner()/rdeps() derivation cannot model (build config, toolchains, vendored third-party, Starlark macros, the lockfile): any touch escalates to the FULL workspace, mechanically, with no skip and no human judgment. require_owner_patterns are the classes that MUST map to an owning target; an existing file in these classes with no owner FAILS the lane (graph-invisible code is not made safe by running more targets).
_full_trigger_note: Two seam classes here. (1) Build config/macros whose blast radius the per-package rdeps cone cannot bound — .buckconfig + .buckconfig.local + .buckconfig.d/** (all read by buck2, all committable), build/toolchains/** + retired toolchains/**, third-party/** (reindeer vendor + fixups), Starlark **/*.bzl + **/*.bxl, rust-toolchain.toml. (2) Buildfiles and PACKAGE files are handled by package_definition_basenames (escalate to FULL on any change) AND mirrored here as **/PACKAGE so a NEW PACKAGE file (which evaluates to [] and would otherwise look like a plain no-owner file) is never a silent no-op. Cargo.lock is deliberately NOT a trigger: buck2 never reads it — a dependency change that affects buck2 semantics MUST touch third-party/**; the cargo lanes + ADR-0539 freshness gate own lock hygiene.
_package_sibling_note: Cargo.toml + build.rs are NOT buck2 graph inputs (buck2 never reads them; reindeer/BUCK mirror them) and have no owner() BY DESIGN, so requiring an owner would refuse every manifest edit (proven by this lane's own first dogfood run). They are semantically bound to their crate, so they seed the ENCLOSING package target pattern; if that package does not exist the seed query fails and the lane escalates to FULL.
_package_definition_note: Ground-truth buck2 buildfile-name set in PRECEDENCE order: BUCK.v2 SHADOWS BUCK when both exist (empirically verified against this buck2 binary — adding an empty BUCK.v2 next to a real BUCK drops the BUCK targets). A change to ANY buildfile escalates to FULL (these basenames are also escape-class): a buildfile edit can add/remove targets or shadow the file dependents load, so its blast radius is NOT bounded by its own package's rdeps. owner() is empty for a buildfile by design, so seeding 'its package' alone would silently miss every dependent (F2). If buck2's [buildfile] name/extra_for_test config ever adds names, mirror them here — this list IS the repo's buildfile-name ground truth, not a single hand-set name.
_synthetic_dependencies_note: ADR-0554 round-6 (defect 2): every changed path must map to a buck2 owner() OR an explicit synthetic-dependency declaration here, otherwise it escalates to FULL (an unowned, undeclared path is derivation uncertainty — the old silent 'docs class — fine' default was a selector hole). Each key is a micro-glob; the value is the list of synthetic seed targets the path contributes (a whole-tree-scanner input declared as a graph edge). An EMPTY list is an explicit inert declaration: 'this class is not a buck2 graph input.' A declaration is ADDITIVE: it UNIONS with owner() rather than applying only when owner() is EMPTY. An owner proves a path is a graph input; it does NOT prove the owner's rdeps cone reaches every target that READS the path, and adr-citation-closure / k8s-program-docs are the standing counter-examples (whole-tree census, own package untouched by an edit). An EMPTY list still contributes no seed, so declaring a class inert never shadows a real owner — an owned instance is still seeded by owner() either way. Package-sibling manifests (`Cargo.toml` / `build.rs`) never enter owner_paths; resolve() still unions synthetic declarations for PathClass::PackagePattern so manifest-only leaf edits (e.g. os/**/Cargo.toml) select their census gates. CONSERVATIVE by design: EVERYTHING unowned and undeclared (yaml/toml/json/txt config, unknown extensions) escalates to FULL until a class earns an evidence-backed declaration. Broadening this map is an optimization follow-up, never a soundness requirement. HISTORICAL CORRECTION (bead oyatie-1ld): this note previously claimed declarations applied only when owner() is empty, and earlier still declared docs/markdown `[]` — both were FALSE; see `_docs_and_markdown_seed_note` and `_k8s_port_census_seed_note`.
_github_seed_note: `.github/**` is the canonical whole-tree-scanner input: owner() is empty for it BY DEFINITION (it is nobody's declared src), which is the PREMISE of a synthetic declaration, not evidence of inertness. Two cheaper shapes were tried and reverted. (1) Declaring it INERT (`[]`) is a FALSE GREEN — a dozen gate tests read `.github/**` at runtime by climbing from cwd to a repo-root marker, and a workflow-only PR resolved to NoGraphTargets and walked past the no-new-shell ratchet (PR #1389, reverted by #1391). (2) Making it OWNED (export_file + $(location)) was ALSO wrong at the time, and for a reason since fixed at the root: resolve() SHORT-CIRCUITED on a non-empty owner() (`seeds.extend(owners); continue`) and never reached synthetic_seeds(), so owning these paths DISABLED this mechanism for them and narrowed the cone to the export's own rdeps. Synthetic declarations are now ADDITIVE (they union with owner()), so ownership no longer suppresses the declaration and this hazard is closed for every class in this map, not just `.github/**`. Declaring the seeds here remains the right shape regardless: it states the live-tree edge explicitly instead of leaving coverage to an export's incidental rdeps. The seeds below are PACKAGE patterns, not individual targets: a package pattern is robust to target renames and is a strict SUPERSET of the specific test targets that read the tree — over-seeding costs build time, under-seeding is a merge-authority hole. The list is not hand-trusted: ci-affected-target-set-github-consumer-coverage derives the consumer set FROM THE TREE (a quote-anchored `.github` path literal in a .rs/.json under a rust_test-bearing buck2 package) and fails closed on any package missing here, so consumer N+1 cannot land unwired. `.gitignore` and `.gitattributes` are deliberately NOT declared — no consumer was verified for them, so they keep escalating to FULL (the safe default). `**/OWNERS` WAS in that undeclared set and has since earned its own evidence-backed declaration; see `_owners_seed_note`. ONE seed is deliberately un-derivable and must not be deleted just because the completeness gate stays green without it: root//ci/facade/artifact-inventory-registry: (the accounting producer) names no `.github` literal at all — it consumes `git ls-files` verbatim, so every tracked `.github` path becomes an accounting row and an add/remove/edit there can flip ci-baseline-ratchet-gate through the frozen baseline + signoff. Its cone was measured to be a strict subset of the derived seeds' cone (zero added targets), so pinning it makes that coverage explicit at zero build cost instead of accidental. UN-DERIVABLE CLASS, enumerated deliberately: five packages consume `git ls-files` verbatim rather than naming a `.github` literal, so the completeness gate can never derive them. `artifact-inventory-registry`, `scm-facts-snapshot` (src/lib.rs:3527, tracked-paths universe moved verbatim from the producer's old git_ls_files), `artifact-accountability`, `crate-registration`, and `inventory-registry-drift` all flow a tracked `.github` add/remove/edit into accounting rows and can flip `ci-baseline-ratchet-gate`. Four of them are in the cone TODAY only transitively, via a dependency edge on a declared seed — exactly the accidental coverage this note rejects, and ADR-0552's scm-facts/accounting split is actively refactoring that edge. Measured cost of pinning all five: ZERO added targets (each already in the cone). Pinning converts accidental coverage into stated coverage at no build cost.
_k8s_port_census_seed_note: FOREVER SHAPE: `os/**/*.rs`, `k8s/**/*.rs`, `os/**/Cargo.toml`, and `k8s/**/Cargo.toml` seed `ci-k8s-program-docs-gate` because that gate equality-pins an INV-3 upstream-apiVersion census over those scan roots. Docs/markdown are NO LONGER whole-tree citation seeds (PROCESS_TAX DELETE 2026-08-11) — do not re-add **/*.md → adr-citation-closure.
_owners_seed_note: `**/OWNERS` is the governance-marker class, declared after PR #1473 — a ONE-LINE diff adding `os/OWNERS` — escalated to FULL and burned 42 minutes before its runner died. Same PREMISE as `.github/**`: owner() is empty because an OWNERS file is nobody's declared src, it is a whole-tree-scanner INPUT. NOT INERT, and the distinction is the whole point: `[]` asserts 'affects no buck2 target', and OWNERS is a live input to the machinery that JUDGES it — artifact-inventory-registry resolves the nearest up-tree OWNERS for every tracked path and validates the file's content schema + breadth bound; baseline-ratchet carries tc-FW-bad-owners-addition-orphans-signoff-entry / tc-FW-good-owners-addition-with-entry-retired firewall fixtures; automation-language-policy asserts the retirement control plane HAS an OWNERS boundary and that `registry/OWNERS` does NOT exist; libs/oya-ci-config holds the `[owners]` marker name + breadth bound as data; libs/oya-crate-registrar-{kernel,app} WRITE `<dir>/OWNERS` during born-accounting. An OWNERS-only PR declared inert would select nothing and skip precisely the gates that judge it — the reverted PR #1389 shape. So the class is declared with REAL seeds, and it is deliberately absent from inert_selection_classes. COMPLETENESS, and why the `.github` gate does not drop in: ci-affected-target-set-github-consumer-coverage derives its list via scan_path_literal_consumers, which keys on a repo-root DIRECTORY prefix (needle `"<class_dir>`). OWNERS is a BASENAME class over 109 directories, so that scan both MISSES real consumers (`".omc/ultragoal/OWNERS"` does not start with `"OWNERS`) and ADMITS coincidental hits (`"OWNERS:{dir}"`, an owner-map value) — an under-approximating scan would rubber-stamp this list, which is worse than no gate. The classes are CHAINED instead: both are whole-tree accounting inputs, so ci-affected-target-set-fixtures asserts this list is a SUPERSET of the `.github/**` list, and the derived gate that keeps THAT list complete transitively keeps this one from rotting. The three seeds beyond that superset are the OWNERS-specific consumers, pinned by name. `LICENSE` was measured in the same shape and deliberately NOT declared here: one tracked instance, effectively never touched, and a different consumer (repo-root-hygiene judges the ROOT allowlist, not a nested copy) — it keeps escalating to FULL, the safe default, until it earns its own evidence-backed line. Same for `.gitignore` / `.gitattributes`.
_docs_and_markdown_seed_note: PROCESS_TAX DELETE (audit 79f76050 / Fail-class law 2026-08-11): once hand files_scanned/citation_lines equality died as a merge blocker, seeding every `**/*.md` into check-adr-citation-closure (and the whole-tree accounting fanout) became pure CI tax with no unique Profile A signal. docs/** / **/*.md / **/*.mdx are again declared synthetic [] + inert_selection_classes so a docs-only diff resolves NoGraphTargets. Semantic citation oracle still runs when the governance package itself (or a real graph owner) is affected — not on every markdown edit. Historical oyatie-1ld / PR #1623 incident applied only while equality pins were merge blockers; that premise is gone.
_baseline_repair_control_plane_seed_note: PR #1486 exposed a baseline-restoration deadlock: six exact unowned registry/spec paths forced FULL, while the clean merge-base materializer failed on the stale artifact path the candidate repaired. These paths are NOT inert. Artifact/dependency rows have live readers; decision-rights and forbidden-operations name their mechanical enforcement packages but are not yet parsed directly by those packages, an explicit semantic-coverage gap rather than a readiness claim. All six feed SCM/generated-face accounting. Common seeds are exact leaf gates, pinned directly instead of relying on today's transitive rdeps edges. The package-wide/library seeds that reach the dev CLI were measured and rejected here because their reverse-dependency closure selects the loop-recovery test, which recursively invokes Cargo across the workspace even though it does not read these inputs. Path-specific leaf seeds add live readers, declared enforcers, or the contract-slice gate. The declaration is intentionally exact-path only: an unknown unowned JSON path still escalates to FULL until its consumers are evidenced.
_inert_selection_classes_note: PREDICATE (1) of the selection-totality assertion: a NON-EMPTY diff that selects NO targets is a target-determination bug, never a pass — the lane would report success having built and tested NOTHING, i.e. green precisely BECAUSE it checked nothing. This list is the ONLY licence for that outcome: a diff consisting solely of these classes may legitimately select nothing. It used to name the docs/markdown classes; see `_docs_licence_revocation_note` for why that was a merge-authority hole and why they were removed. It is deliberately NOT derived from the `[]` entries in synthetic_dependencies, because those two statements differ — `synthetic_dependencies[X] = []` says 'X contributes no seed', this list says 'X may be the ENTIRE selection and still pass'. PR #1389 is the proof the split matters: `.github/**: []` was defensible as the first statement and a merge-authority hole as the second (a workflow-only PR resolved to NoGraphTargets and walked past the no-new-shell ratchet). With the split, adding a broad class to synthetic_dependencies as `[]` now FAILS RED naming the path instead of passing green; granting it an empty selection takes a second, single-purpose, reviewed line here. GROWING THIS LIST IS A MERGE-AUTHORITY CHANGE — an entry asserts the class can affect NO buck2 target whatsoever, and being wrong is silent. Absent field = empty = fail-closed (any non-empty diff that selects nothing is refused).
_evidence_reorg_inert_note: R-DUAL-0615: evidence/reorg/** is inventory/disposition evidence only; not a buck2 graph input. Markdown under it is covered by the restored **/*.md inert licence (PROCESS_TAX DELETE 2026-08-11); JSON remains synthetic [] + inert.
_docs_licence_revocation_note: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-11 by Fail-class law / audit 79f76050: docs/markdown classes AGAIN hold the empty-selection licence (see inert_selection_classes). The oyatie-1ld revocation was correct while equality-pinned census was a merge blocker; with that PROCESS_TAX deleted, restoring NoGraphTargets for docs-only is the tip-entitlement law (docs-only / re-freeze commits get no CI entitlement).

product_contract.born_pack_shaped: The escape-trigger classes, owner-required classes, universe, full-run patterns, cell roots, and base ref are DATA here; the Rust kernel hardcodes no repo path nor any oyatie string (R0, ADR-0548). The kernel DOES fix the decision SEMANTICS — RefuseUnowned > Full > Affected > NoGraphTargets dominance, derivation-uncertainty-escalates-to-full, owner() on every existing changed file regardless of extension — that contract is the engine, not a per-repo pack value.
product_contract.fail_closed: Derivation NEVER skips: git/uquery/rdeps errors, unmappable package files, deleted graph files, and empty rdeps closures all escalate to the full workspace run. The only hard failures are an unreadable/invalid pack, owner-required files with no owning target, and the build/test verdict itself.
product_contract.tiers: pull_request -> auto (affected cone, escalation binding); merge_group + push + workflow_dispatch -> full (admission/integration tier per ADR-0515 Tide direction).
product_contract.precedent: Bazel target determination / bazel-diff (Tinder), Meta/Google affected-target CI; reimplemented Rust-native on buck2 uquery owner()/rdeps() per the proven-patterns doctrine.
product_contract.execution: Buck2-native Rust lane; no shell logic beyond the workflow YAML step (G011 Rust-successor that RETIRED the transitional infra/ci/buck2-affected-gate.sh shell driver, removed ADR-0554 round-6).

purpose: Binding workspace coverage: every PR builds+tests the buck2 reverse-dependency cone of its merge-base diff as a REQUIRED context, with mechanical fail-closed escalation to the full workspace whenever the cone cannot be trusted. Any owner-required source change with a buck2 target builds+tests its cone; any buildfile/config/macro change escalates to FULL; a genuinely-unowned owner-required file (e.g. a source in a sub-workspace buck2 does not model) REFUSES the merge until it is wired — never silently passes.
